newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ deer company plans NZ$20 million float.
newsitem.headline: NZ deer company plans NZ$20 million float.

text.p: New Zealand Deer Farms, owned by interests associated with Tasman Agriculture founder Howard Paterson, plans a $20 million float in March, the New Zealand Herald reported on Wednesday.
Some of the cash will be used to buy the existing deer farms, leaving Paterson and associated parties with about a 43 percent holding.
Paterson, contacted by telephone, confirmed the company was planning a float and had a draft prospectus, but declined to confirm details.
The company is expected to have a capitalisation of $35 million, the Herald said.
The provisional listing date is March 7 with the prospectus due to be released on February 14. The offer, which will not have a public pool, will open on February 17.
Deer company Eastern Deer floated in 1985 but after a rocky path transformed itself into fruit grower Eastern Equities.
By 2000, New Zealand Deer Farms hopes to be producing 1.6 million kg of venison a year, around six percent of New Zealand's production, and have 31,500 breeding hinds.
This is forecast to generate an annual tax-paid profit of $4.5 million, earnings per share of 13 cents and a dividend of just under 10 cents.
The 1998 year profit is forecast to be $1.5 million, rising to $3.8 million in 1999.
The company plans to have three properties totalling around 11,600 hectares and has earmarked three South Island properties for purchase and conversion to deer farms, the report said.
Company chairman will be Phil Pryke, and other directors will be Sir Peter Elworthy, David Smallbone and Paterson.
